title: Gnostic Lineage
subtitle: From the Monad to Adam & Eve — the emanation of the Fullness and the fall into the world

nodes.name: The Monad
nodes.aka: The Invisible Virgin Spirit · The One
nodes.definition: The ineffable Source of all -- the utterly transcendent One beyond being, name, and thought. Not a god among gods but the Root from which the whole Fullness flows; complete in itself and needing nothing. Within the Monad the Father, as He is named and made apparent, dwells -- the Monad's own self-manifestation, the face by which the unknowable One is known.
nodes.appearance: Formless and invisible: 'not corporeal, not incorporeal; not great, not small.' It is beheld only as boundless pure light and living water surrounding itself; no image can contain it.
nodes.nature: Perfect, immeasurable, eternal, self-sufficient. It creates not from lack or desire but overflows in pure grace, contemplating its own light. The apparent Father dwells within it, so that the hidden Source and the revealed Father are one.

nodes.name: Barbelo
nodes.aka: First Thought · the Mother-Father · Pronoia
nodes.definition: The first emanation of the Invisible Spirit -- its own reflection made real -- the primal Forethought (Pronoia) and Mother of all who come after; the first power and perfect glory in whom the All is conceived.
nodes.appearance: A luminous image of the Spirit, androgynous and perfect: the triple-male, triple-powered, invisible aeon shining as the Spirit's own mirror.
nodes.nature: The womb of the entirety, first to receive being -- Mother-Father at once: the Father's thought and the Mother of the Aeons.

nodes.definition: Begotten of Barbelo by the Spirit's spark -- the Self-Generated One, the only-begotten Son, the anointed Christ -- through whom the aeons are established and ordered.
nodes.appearance: The divine child crowned by the Invisible Spirit, shining with the light of the four luminaries; the perfected, self-arising radiance.
nodes.nature: True and perfect Son, mind of the All, given power to establish the aeons and set the luminaries in place.

nodes.name: The Four Luminaries
nodes.aka: Harmozel · Oroiael · Davithe · Eleleth
nodes.definition: Four great lights set around the Autogenes -- each a heavenly aeon housing grace, understanding, perception, and prudence, and each the dwelling of one rank of the holy race. To each luminary three attendant aeons are joined, so that twelve aeons in all wait upon the Son.
nodes.appearance: Four radiant thrones or standing lights encircling the Son, each with its own attendant powers.
nodes.nature: The dwelling-places of the perfect: Harmozel of Adamas, Oroiael of Seth, Davithe of Seth's seed, and Eleleth, where the souls who repented late are gathered.

nodes.name: Yaldabaoth
nodes.aka: Ialdabaoth · Saklas · Samael · the Demiurge
nodes.definition: Sophia's misbegotten offspring, brought forth without a consort -- the Demiurge, chief Archon, the ignorant creator of the material cosmos who declares 'I am God, and there is no other,' not knowing the Fullness above him.
nodes.appearance: A monstrous form: a serpent with the face of a lion, his eyes flashing like lightning-fire; Sophia hides him in a luminous cloud, apart from the immortals.
nodes.nature: Arrogant, blind (Samael, 'the blind god'), jealous and foolish (Saklas). He fashions the lower world and its rulers as a dim shadow of what is above.

nodes.name: The Archons
nodes.aka: the Authorities · the Rulers · the Seven & the Twelve
nodes.definition: The powers Yaldabaoth brings forth to govern matter. He begets TWELVE authorities and sets SEVEN kings over the seven heavens (each with a beast's face) and five over the abyss, sharing his stolen fire with them but not the light. To each of the seven he joins one of seven powers -- goodness, foreknowledge, divinity, lordship, kingdom, zeal, and understanding -- so that his imitation heaven mirrors the Fullness above in a dim, ignorant copy. Together they administer fate (heimarmene) over the lower creation. (The Apocryphon of John gives TWO overlapping rosters: the twelve authorities begotten of Yaldabaoth, and the seven animal-faced kings who are the 'bodies belonging with the names' -- both are set out below.)
nodes.appearance: Beast-faced, animal-headed rulers, each set over a heaven or a passion; Yaldabaoth himself wears a multitude of faces and can set any face before them at will.
nodes.nature: Blind servants of the Demiurge, imitating the powers above and binding souls under fate. 'In the names given to them by their Originator there was power.'

nodes.definition: Enoch son of Jared, taken up and transformed into the greatest of the angels — viceroy over all the host of heaven, prince over all the princes save the eight great princes called YHWH, and the Lesser YHWH in whom the Name dwells (3 Enoch 10, 12, 48C). nodes.appearance: Enlarged to the size of the length and breadth of the world, with 72 wings — each wing as wide as the whole world — and 365 eyes, each as great as the great luminary; his stature and his throne of fire seventy thousand parasangs, his crown five hundred by five hundred parasangs (3 Enoch 9, 48C).
nodes.nature: The 'Youth' (Na'ar), least and youngest made greatest; bearer of seventy names for the seventy tongues, and of the crown on which the letters by which heaven and earth were sealed are graven. 'My name is in him' (Exodus 23:21).

nodes.name: The Great Chief Princes
nodes.aka: over the Seraphim, Ophannim, Kerubim, Chayyoth & the wheels
nodes.definition: The mighty princes set each over one order of the living chariot, in the text's own 'above these there is one prince' ascent — from Rikbiel over the wheels up to Radweriel, out of whose every word an angel is created (3 Enoch 19–27), with the two scribe-princes Sopheriel who write the books of the living and the dead.
nodes.appearance: Each as high as the seven heavens, their bodies full of eyes; Seraphiel's head-sapphire as great as the whole universe (3 Enoch 26).

members.name: Radweriel
members.definition: Exalted above all the princes, keeper of the treasuries of the books; he brings the Case of Writings before God. Called Radweriel because out of every word that goes forth from his mouth an angel is created.
members.appearance: Wondrous beyond all the servants.

members.name: Seraphiel
members.place: height as the seven heavens · 3 Enoch 26
members.definition: Appointed over the Seraphim; a chief, leader and swift scribe. His crown is named 'the Prince of Peace.' The Seraphim are so called because they burn (saraph) the tablets of Satan.
members.appearance: His height as the seven heavens; his body like an eagle's; the sapphire on his head as great as the universe; his crown a journey of 502 years.

members.name: Rikbiel
members.roster: Prince over the wheels of the Merkaba
members.definition: Set above the three chariot-princes; appointed over the wheels (rekeb) of the Merkaba, like whom there is none among the princes.
members.appearance: Chief of the chariot-wheels.
members.nature: The chariot moves at his charge.

members.name: Sopheriel who kills
members.definition: One of the two great scribe-princes; appointed over the books of the dead — he writes a man into the book of the dead.
members.appearance: Height as seven heavens; body full of eyes; wings as the days of the year; his burning scroll and style 3000 myriads of parasangs, each letter he writes 365 parasangs.

members.name: Sopheriel who makes alive
members.definition: The second great scribe-prince; appointed over the books of the living — he writes a man into the book of life, by the authority of MAQOM.
members.appearance: As his fellow: seven-heaven height, letters of 365 parasangs.

nodes.name: The Crown-Removal Ladder
nodes.aka: the princes who bow, each to the one above
nodes.definition: A descending file of princes, each of whom 'removes the crown of glory from his head and falls on his face' before the prince above him (3 Enoch 18) — the very picture of the hierarchy: every rank bows to the greater. Listed here greatest first.
nodes.appearance: Crowned princes prostrate in order, the least casting down his crown before the next.
nodes.nature: The order of homage — each honours the one set over him.

members.name: 'Azbuga
members.definition: Just below the two Sopheriel; in the age to come he will gird the righteous with garments of life.
members.appearance: A prince before the scribes.

members.name: Zehanpuryu
members.definition: He rebukes the fiery river and pushes it back.
members.appearance: Master of the river of fire.

members.name: Shoqed Chozi
members.definition: He weighs all the merits of man in a balance.
members.appearance: Holder of the scales.

members.name: Sother 'Ashiel
members.definition: Appointed over the four heads of the fiery river; its seals are entrusted to him.
members.appearance: His height seven thousand myriads of parasangs.

members.name: 'Anaphiel
members.definition: The prince who keeps the keys of the heavenly Halls; named because the bough (anaph) of his honour overshadows all the chambers of 'Araboth. He it is who bears Enoch aloft on a fiery chariot (3 Enoch 6).
members.appearance: His majesty a spreading bough over all the highest heaven.

members.name: Zakzakiel
members.definition: Appointed to write down the merits of Israel upon the Throne of Glory.
members.appearance: Scribe at the Throne.

members.name: Gallisur
members.definition: He reveals all the secrets of the Torah.
members.appearance: Unveiler of the Law.

members.name: 'Ashruylu
members.definition: He presides in all the sessions of the children of heaven.
members.appearance: Chair of the heavenly councils.

members.name: 'Araphiel, Geburatiel, Zazriel, Sasnigiel
members.definition: Four great princes of the ladder named by their titles in order — 'Araphiel, Geburatiel (of might), Zazriel, Sasnigiel — each bowing to the one above.
members.appearance: Crowned princes in file.

members.name: Na'aririel, Atrugiel, Tutresiel
members.definition: Three princes of the lower ladder, named in their turn.
members.appearance: Crowned princes in file.

members.name: Hamon
members.definition: The fearful prince who makes all the children of heaven tremble at the hour of the Thrice-Holy — named from hamon, 'tumult' (Isaiah 33:3).
members.appearance: At his voice the host quakes.

members.name: Barattiel
members.definition: The great prince who bears up the height of 'Araboth upon three fingers.
members.appearance: Three fingers upholding the highest heaven.

members.name: Tag'as
members.definition: Great and honoured with song and praise, at the head of all the children of heaven — before whom the four princes of the Camps of Shekina bow.
members.appearance: Leader of the heavenly song.

nodes.name: The Camps, Halls & Kingdoms
nodes.aka: the rungs of homage — camps, hall-keepers, the 72 princes
nodes.definition: The lower rungs of the ladder (3 Enoch 17–18, 30): the four great princes over the Camps of the Shekina; the door-keepers of the seven Halls, each bowing to the next-higher Hall; the seventy-two Princes of the Kingdoms for the seventy-two tongues; and the Prince of the World who pleads for the world before God.
nodes.appearance: Crowned princes riding royal horses with sceptres; door-keepers ranged from the seventh Hall down to the first.
nodes.nature: The governance of the nations and the guard of the Halls.

members.name: The four princes of the Camps of Shekina
members.definition: Four great princes set over the four camps of the Shekina, before whom the door-keepers of the seventh Hall bow.
members.appearance: Guardians of the four camps.

members.name: The door-keepers of the seven Halls
members.definition: The keepers of the seven Halls (Hekhalot); those of each Hall remove their crowns before those of the next-higher Hall, up to the Four Camps.
members.appearance: Keepers ranged from the first Hall to the seventh.

members.name: The seventy-two Princes of Kingdoms
members.definition: Seventy-two princes set over the seventy-two kingdoms and tongues of the world — crowned, on royal horses, with royal sceptres — before whom the prince of the seventh heaven bows.
members.appearance: Kings crowned and sceptred.
members.nature: The angelic governors of the nations.

members.name: The Prince of the World
members.definition: The prince who pleads in the world's favour before the Holy One each day when the book is opened, and who quiets the trembling heavenly bodies — 'Be ye quiet in your place!'
members.appearance: Advocate before the Throne.
members.nature: Steward and pleader of the created world.

nodes.name: The Seven Princes of the Heavens
nodes.aka: Mikael, Gabriel & the archangels
nodes.definition: Seven princes, one over each of the seven heavens, each with hundreds of thousands of myriads of ministering angels (3 Enoch 17); Mikael the prince of Israel is highest, in 'Araboth. Joined here by the seven archangels who stand before the Lord in 1 Enoch — Michael, Gabriel, Raphael, Uriel, Raguel, Saraqael, Remiel.
nodes.appearance: Each attended by 496,000 myriads of ministering angels.
nodes.nature: The wardens of the seven heavens and the presence.

nodes.name: The Luminary Princes, the Living Orders & the Fallen
nodes.aka: sun, moon, stars, the Chayyoth, and the Watchers who fell
nodes.definition: The lowest ranks of the exalted host: the princes of the luminaries (sun, moon, stars, planets), the eighteen rulers of the natural world, and the four living orders that bear and surround the Throne — the Chayyoth, Kerubim, Ophannim and Seraphim — each as vast as the world. Set apart beneath them, the Watchers who fell and the accusers.
nodes.appearance: Each living creature as the space of the whole world, each wing like the roof of the universe; the moon-prince moving the moon 354,000 parasangs a night.
nodes.nature: The engines of day and night, and the four faces of the chariot — with the fallen shown below, apart.

members.name: The eighteen rulers of the world
members.aka: Baradiel · Ruchiel · Baraqiel · Za'amiel · Ziqiel · Zi'iel · Za'aphiel · Ra'amiel · Ra'ashiel · Shalgiel · Matariel · Shimshiel · Lailiel …
members.place: wind, hail, lightning, snow, rain, thunder, day & night
members.definition: The eighteen princes set over the forces of nature — Ruchiel (wind), Baradiel (hail), Baraqiel (lightning), Ra'amiel (thunder), Ra'ashiel (earthquake), Shalgiel (snow), Matariel (rain), Shimshiel (day), Lailiel (night), and the rest — all of whom trembled before Metatron when he was crowned (3 Enoch 14).
members.appearance: The storm-angels of the sky.
members.nature: The governance of weather and season.

members.name: The Holy Chayyoth
members.place: each as the whole world · 3 Enoch 21
members.definition: The four Living Creatures that bear the Throne — four faces and four wings each; each Chayya as the space of the whole world, each wing like the roof of the universe, with 2000 crowns on each head.
members.appearance: World-wide living creatures beneath the Throne.
